chunks: “There is no mutual liability among the Ahl al-Dhimmah for what they commit of killing or injury. Rather, that is taken from their own property; and if they do not have property, the liability returns to the Imam of the Muslims, because they pay the jizyah to him just as a slave pays tax to his master.” He said: “And they are owned dependents of the Imam, so whoever among them embraces Islam, he is free.”
And (675) 15 — Ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from his father, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said:

A man who had killed another man by mistake was brought to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام. Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said to him: “Who are your clan and your relatives?” He said: “I have no clan or relatives in this town.” He said: “From which land are you?” He said: “I am a man from the people of al-Mawsil; I was born there, and I have relatives and household there.” He said: So Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام inquired about him, and he did not find for him in al-Kufah any relatives or clan.

He said: So he wrote to his governor over al-Mawsil: “Now then, so-and-so son of so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such, has killed a Muslim man by mistake. He mentioned that he is a man from the people of al-Mawsil and that he has relatives and household there. I have sent him to you with my messenger so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such. When he arrives to you, Allah willing, and you have read my letter, investigate his matter and ask about his Muslim relatives. If he is from the people of al-Mawsil, among those born there, and you find for him there Muslim relatives, then gather them to yourself. Then see: if among them there is a man who inherits him, having an apportioned share in the Book, not barred from his inheritance by any of his relatives, then impose the diyah upon him and collect it from him in installments over three years.”

And if he has no one among his relatives who has an apportioned share in the Book, and they are relatives equal in lineage, and he has relatives from his father’s side and his mother’s side equal in lineage, then distribute the diyah among his relatives from his father’s side and among his relatives from his mother’s side, from the adult Muslim men. Then assign to his relatives from his father’s side two-thirds of the diyah, and assign to his relatives from his mother’s side one-third of the diyah.

And if he has no relatives from his father’s side, then distribute the diyah among his relatives from his mother’s side, from the adult men; then bind them to it and exact the diyah from them over three years.

And if he has no relatives from his father’s side and no relatives from his mother’s side, then distribute the diyah among the people of al-Mawsil who were born there and raised there, and do not include among them anyone else from the people of the town. Then exact that from them over three years, one installment in each year, until you fully collect it, if Allah wills.

And if so-and-so son of so-and-so has no relatives from the people of al-Mawsil, and is not from its people, and is false in his claim, then send him back to me with my messenger so-and-so, for I am his guardian and the one who will pay on his behalf; and the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left without recompense.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: non-Muslim protected subjects living under Islamic rule
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money compensation owed for wrongful killing or injury
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةَ: poll-tax paid by Ahl al-Dhimmah to the Islamic authority
key_terms.الْجِنَايَةُ: offense entailing legal liability, such as killing or injury
key_terms.قَرَابَتِهِ: his kinship relatives through whom liability is assessed
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his legal guardian or authority responsible for him

ai.seo_question: How is diyah assigned in cases of accidental killing when the killer has no local relatives or clan?
ai.summary: This report sets out legal rulings concerning liability for wrongful killing and injury, especially regarding Ahl al-Dhimmah and cases of accidental killing. It details how diyah is assigned through kinship relations, local affiliation, and ultimately the authority of the Imam, ensuring that the blood of a Muslim is not left uncompensated.
